prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (within 500 words, policy-focused, no ideological framing or names)

- Europe and Brexit: Proposes a referendum on the negotiated EU deal with an option to remain. Seeks close EU ties including single market and customs union participation; guarantees for EU and UK citizens’ rights; protection of freedom of movement benefits; Erasmus+ and youth opportunities; maintenance of social, environmental, policing and judicial cooperation; safeguarding research funding, business access, travel benefits, and devolved nations’ interests.

- NHS and social care: Immediate 1p rise on Income Tax (and equivalent on dividends) ringfenced for health and care; plan for a dedicated health and care tax; independent budget watchdog for health/care; cross-party convention on long-term sustainability; integrate health and social care with pooled budgets by 2020; cap social care costs. Workforce measures include ending public sector pay cap, restoring nurse bursaries, guaranteeing EU staff rights, national workforce strategy. Mental health parity with waiting-time standards, expanded talking therapies, perinatal and crisis care, ending out-of-area placements.

- Public health and community care: Easier GP access (evenings/weekends, digital appointments), support for struggling practices, multidisciplinary hubs, fair prescription exemptions. Prevention: antimicrobial resistance plan, PrEP on NHS, obesity strategy (advertising and sugar measures), tobacco levy, minimum unit alcohol pricing (subject to outcomes), wellbeing promotion.

- Education and skills: Nearly £7bn extra over a parliament; real-terms per-pupil protection; fair funding formula without losers; protect and expand Pupil Premium; oppose new selective schools; restore local authority role in places planning. Early years: triple Early Years Pupil Premium, raise quality. Teachers: end 1% pay cap; funded professional development; workload and Ofsted reform. Curriculum: slimmed core including PSHE, financial literacy, first aid, mental health, SRE (including consent and LGBT+ content); protect arts; improve vocational routes and careers advice; strengthen employer links; early SEN support. Pupil wellbeing: staff training, school counselling, free primary lunches and breakfast clubs. Universities: reinstate maintenance grants; review finance; widen participation; protect international collaboration and funding. Lifelong learning: expand apprenticeships, national colleges, adult learning accounts, basic skills by 2030.

- Economy and tax: Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; £100bn infrastructure plan (300,000 homes/year by 2022, hyperfast fibre, schools/hospitals, rail incl. HS2/Crossrail 2, renewables, new housing/infrastructure bank). Reverse selected tax cuts; tackle avoidance (general anti-avoidance rule, corporate tax reform, business rates review, consider land value tax); fair intergenerational review. SMEs: expand British Business Bank, start-up allowance, mentoring, reduce regulatory burdens. Innovation: protect and grow science budget; broadband FTTP as standard; digital skills; support creative and green tech. Work: living-wage roadmap, curb exploitative zero-hours, strengthen enforcement, transparency on pay; promote employee ownership and worker participation.

- Environment: Five green laws; retrofit insulation for 4m homes by 2022; air quality plan (diesel scrappage; end sale of diesel cars/small vans by 2025; expand ultra-low-emission zones; accelerate charging infrastructure). Energy: net-zero by 2050; 60% electricity from renewables by 2030; support storage, smart grids, hydrogen, offshore wind, tidal (incl. Swansea Bay), CCS; oppose fracking; conditional nuclear; remain in Euratom. Green buildings: restore zero-carbon homes; community energy; diversify suppliers. Nature: £2bn flood fund; statutory natural capital targets; expand accessible green space; tree planting; protect waters and marine areas; stronger animal welfare. Farming/fisheries: refocus support on public goods and smaller farms; fair supply chains; national food strategy; high import standards; TB vaccines; defend sustainable fisheries. Waste: circular economy targets; 70% recycling by 2022; coffee cup charge; landfill/incineration reform.

- Families, welfare, housing, transport: Childcare from 9 months for working parents (phased), 15–30 hours goals; extra month shared parental leave; day-one flexible working. Welfare: uprate working-age benefits; reverse selected cuts; scrap bedroom tax; winter fuel means-tested; retain pension triple lock. Housing: 300,000 homes/year, 10+ garden cities, end barriers to council/social building, planning reforms, powers on empty/second homes; renting reforms (ban letting fees, cap deposits, longer tenancies, Help to Rent loans, tenants’ first refusal). Transport: rail franchise reform with public bids, electrification, HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2, freight to rail, regional strategies, bus regulation powers, youth bus discount, cycling/walking investment; regional airport focus.

- Rights, justice, immigration: Make all hate crimes aggravated offences; retain Human Rights Act/ECHR; expand refugee resettlement (50,000) and child resettlement (3,000); digital bill of rights; press regulation reform; FOI strengthening; £300m for community policing, body cameras, cross-border crime cooperation; presumption against short prison terms; restorative justice; women’s and youth justice reforms; legal aid/fees review. Drugs: decriminalise possession; regulate cannabis; shift lead to Health. Immigration: efficient system with annual skills debate; exclude students from migration stats; restore STEM post-study visas; Migration Impact Fund; ESOL funding; 28-day detention limit; faster asylum processing and safe routes.

- International and defence: Support UN, NATO, rules-based order; maintain 0.7% aid; tighter arms export controls and suspend certain sales; cyber investment; minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced boats/changed posture; support veterans.

- Political reform and devolution: Votes at 16; STV for local and Westminster; Lords reform; donation cap; stronger lobbying rules; weekend voting pilots; fairer expense rules. Constitutional convention toward a federal UK; devolve repatriated powers; enhanced powers for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; English devolution on demand; maintain Barnett with fair funding for Wales.
